mos-small-signal-model.L1: Draws the saturated MOSFET model: a current source g_m·v_gs from drain to source, r_o across it, and no gate current.
mos-small-signal-model.L2: Substitutes the model into a single-transistor circuit and solves it, with g_m and r_o computed from the bias.
mos-small-signal-model.L3: Explains each part: g_m·v_gs is the tangent's slope, r_o = 1/(λI_D) the slope of i_D against v_DS, and the open gate the insulating oxide; says why the model is the same for every circuit while its numbers change with the bias.
mos-small-signal-model.L4: Adds g_mb for a source not at the body potential and the capacitances for high frequency; knows the model holds only in saturation and for v_gs ≪ V_OV.
missteps: adds a resistor between gate and source in the MOSFET model
uses the small-signal model without checking that the transistor is in saturation
draws the current source pointing the wrong way for v_gs
uses r_o = 1/(λI_D) with λ = 0 and gets zero instead of infinity

seeds.predict: Two transistors carry the same current, one at twice the V_OV of the other. Compare their g_m and r_o.
seeds.explain: Why there is no resistor between gate and source in the MOSFET model.
seeds.limit: λ made smaller and smaller: what does r_o become, and what is the transistor then?
seeds.transfer: A PMOS common-source stage with its source on V_DD: draw its small-signal circuit and compare it with the NMOS one.

mos-capacitor.L1: States that a MOS capacitor is a gate on oxide over a doped body, and that an NMOS capacitor has a p-type body.
mos-capacitor.L2: Computes C_ox = ε_ox/t_ox and names the body's charge (holes, ions, electrons) for a given gate voltage.
mos-capacitor.L3: Explains why the body plate is unlike a metal plate: it answers with holes, then depletion, then an electron sheet; splits the gate voltage into V_ox and ψ_s; says why the flavour is named after the inversion carriers.
mos-capacitor.L4: Uses the MOS capacitor to explain the MOSFET's channel charge and its gate capacitance; knows where the simple picture fails (oxide charge, quantum effects, poly depletion in thin oxides).
missteps: calls the body of an NMOS capacitor n-type
puts all of the gate voltage across the oxide
treats the body plate as a metal plate at every voltage

seeds.predict: A gate is raised from just above V_FB to just below V_T: where does the new body charge appear?
seeds.explain: Why the body answers the gate in three different ways depending on its voltage.
seeds.limit: The oxide made very thick: what happens to C_ox, to V_T, and to the share of the voltage across the body?
seeds.transfer: A capacitor on a chip must be linear over a wide voltage range: which region of a MOS capacitor would you bias it in, and why?

accumulation-depletion-inversion.L1: Names the three regimes in order of gate voltage and the body charge in each.
accumulation-depletion-inversion.L2: Decides the regime from V_GB, V_FB and V_T, and computes the charge in accumulation and inversion from C_ox.
accumulation-depletion-inversion.L3: Sketches charge and potential through the stack in each regime; explains why the depletion stops widening at V_T (the electron sheet takes any extra charge, at the surface); computes ψ_s and x_d in depletion.
accumulation-depletion-inversion.L4: Knows the electron density grows exponentially in weak inversion, below V_T, which the charge-sheet model ignores, and why that matters for leakage.
missteps: keeps widening the depletion region above V_T
puts minority carriers in the depletion region
confuses accumulation holes with inversion electrons

seeds.predict: V_GB is raised by 1 V above V_T: how much does x_d change, and how much does Q_inv change?
seeds.explain: Why the depletion region stops growing once the inversion layer forms.
seeds.limit: V_GB far below V_FB: what is the body charge, and where does all the voltage sit?
seeds.transfer: A PMOS capacitor on an n body: describe its three regimes with the signs of the voltages and charges.

threshold-voltage.L1: States V_T = V_FB + 2|φ_p| + |Q_B,max|/C_ox and names each term.
threshold-voltage.L2: Computes V_T from N_A, t_ox and the gate material.
threshold-voltage.L3: Explains each term as a step: cancel the built-in potential, bend the surface by 2|φ_p|, hold the depletion charge across the oxide; predicts how doping, oxide thickness and gate material move V_T.
threshold-voltage.L4: Adds oxide charge and body bias; knows why V_T is set with a threshold implant in practice, and why it falls in short channels.
missteps: uses |φ_p| instead of 2|φ_p|
takes V_FB as zero or with the wrong sign
uses an oxide thickness in nm where cm is needed

seeds.predict: N_A is quadrupled: which terms of V_T change, and does V_T rise or fall?
seeds.explain: Why holding the depletion charge across the oxide costs |Q_B,max|/C_ox of gate voltage.
seeds.limit: The oxide made thinner and thinner: which term of V_T shrinks, and what is V_T heading toward?
seeds.transfer: A designer needs V_T to rise by 0.2 V without changing the oxide: what would they change, and by how much roughly?

flatband-voltage.L1: States V_FB = φ_p − φ_gate (with the course's signs) and that it is the gate voltage that leaves no charge.
flatband-voltage.L2: Computes V_FB for an n+ or p+ poly gate on a given body.
flatband-voltage.L3: Explains V_FB as cancelling the built-in step between gate and body materials; predicts its sign for each gate and body combination.
flatband-voltage.L4: Adds fixed oxide charge to V_FB and knows why gate work function is chosen to set V_T.
missteps: takes V_FB as zero
gets the sign wrong for an n+ gate on a p body
uses φ_p with the wrong sign

seeds.predict: An n+ gate is replaced by a p+ gate on the same body: how does V_FB move, and by how much?
seeds.explain: Why there is charge on a MOS capacitor even with the gate shorted to the body.
seeds.limit: Body doping raised toward degenerate: what happens to φ_p and to V_FB?
seeds.transfer: A metal gate with a work function midway in the gap: estimate V_FB on a given p body.

mos-cv-curve.L1: States that C = C_ox in accumulation and dips in depletion.
mos-cv-curve.L2: Computes the depletion capacitance and the series combination with C_ox at a bias.
mos-cv-curve.L3: Explains C as the slope of charge against voltage; explains the dip (the charge moves deeper) and why inversion returns to C_ox only when measured slowly.
mos-cv-curve.L4: Extracts t_ox, N_A, V_FB and V_T from a measured C–V curve.
missteps: adds C_ox and C_dep in parallel
expects the high-frequency curve to return to C_ox
uses the total charge over voltage instead of the slope

seeds.predict: The doping is raised: what happens to the depth of the dip and to the minimum capacitance?
seeds.explain: Why the capacitance measured fast stays low in inversion.
seeds.limit: V_GB far into accumulation: what does C approach, and what does it tell you?
seeds.transfer: From a measured C–V curve, how would you read off the oxide thickness and the body doping?

mosfet-regions.L1: Names cut-off, triode and saturation and their conditions: V_GS < V_T; V_DS < V_GS − V_T; V_DS ≥ V_GS − V_T.
mosfet-regions.L2: Decides the region from given terminal voltages and picks the right current formula.
mosfet-regions.L3: Explains each region from the channel: no sheet in cut-off; a sheet reaching the drain in triode; a sheet pinched off at the drain in saturation; reads the regions off the output curves and the edge V_DS = V_OV.
mosfet-regions.L4: Checks the region before and after solving a circuit, and guesses a region, solves, then verifies; knows the edges blur in real devices (subthreshold, channel-length modulation).
missteps: compares V_DS with V_GS instead of V_GS − V_T
takes saturation to mean the transistor is fully on
uses a formula before checking the region

seeds.predict: A transistor with V_OV = 0.4 V has its drain lowered from 1 V to 0.2 V: which region is it in, and what happens to I_D?
seeds.explain: Why the boundary between triode and saturation is V_DS = V_GS − V_T and not V_DS = V_GS.
seeds.limit: V_GS lowered toward V_T at fixed V_DS: which region does the transistor end in, and how does it get there?
seeds.transfer: A circuit's transistor is assumed saturated, and the solution gives V_DS = 0.1 V with V_OV = 0.3 V: what was wrong, and what do you do next?

triode-region.L1: States I_D = μC_ox(W/L)[(V_GS − V_T)V_DS − V_DS²/2] for V_DS < V_GS − V_T.
triode-region.L2: Computes the triode current and the on-resistance 1/(μC_ox(W/L)V_OV) for small V_DS.
triode-region.L3: Derives the current as drift of the channel charge C_ox(V_OV − V(x)) and explains the −V_DS²/2 as the sheet thinning toward the drain; explains the transistor as a gate-controlled resistor at small V_DS.
triode-region.L4: Uses a triode transistor as a switch or variable resistor and knows how big the signal can be before its resistance changes; knows the body effect varies V_T along the channel.
missteps: drops the V_DS²/2 term at V_DS comparable to V_OV
takes the channel charge as uniform at large V_DS
uses the triode formula past V_DS = V_OV

seeds.predict: A transistor in deep triode has its V_GS raised by 0.2 V: what happens to its resistance, roughly?
seeds.explain: Why the triode current bends over as V_DS grows.
seeds.limit: V_DS made much smaller than V_OV: what does the transistor become, and what sets its value?
seeds.transfer: A transistor used as an analog switch carries a 0.3 V signal with V_OV = 1 V: how far from constant is its resistance across the swing?

pinch-off.L1: States that pinch-off happens when V_DS = V_GS − V_T, where the channel charge at the drain falls to zero.
pinch-off.L2: Finds V_DS,sat = V_OV for a given bias.
pinch-off.L3: Explains pinch-off as the gate-to-channel voltage at the drain falling to V_T; explains why the current does not stop (a short high-field gap carries it) and why it stops growing.
pinch-off.L4: Knows the gap lengthens with V_DS and shortens the channel (channel-length modulation), and that velocity saturation, not an infinite field, governs the region near the drain.
missteps: thinks pinch-off stops the current
puts the pinch-off condition at V_DS = V_GS
thinks the whole channel vanishes at pinch-off

seeds.predict: V_DS is raised past V_OV by 1 V: where does that extra volt drop, and what happens to I_D?
seeds.explain: Why the drain current keeps flowing through a region with no channel charge.
seeds.limit: The channel made very short: why does the long-channel picture of pinch-off fail?
seeds.transfer: Why does a saturated transistor look like a current source to the drain circuit, and what spoils that?

square-law.L1: States I_D = ½μC_ox(W/L)(V_GS − V_T)² in saturation.
square-law.L2: Computes I_D from V_OV, or V_OV from I_D, and scales the current with W/L and V_OV.
square-law.L3: Explains the square as charge per area times the voltage drifted through, both proportional to V_OV; gets it from the triode formula at V_DS = V_OV; predicts four times the current for twice the overdrive.
square-law.L4: Knows the square law fails with velocity saturation (current more nearly linear in V_OV) and in weak inversion (exponential); uses g_m = 2I_D/V_OV from it.
missteps: forgets the ½
squares V_GS instead of V_GS − V_T
doubles the current for twice the overdrive

seeds.predict: A saturated transistor carries 100 µA at V_OV = 0.2 V: what at 0.3 V, and what at 0.2 V with W doubled?
seeds.explain: Why the saturated current goes as the square of the overdrive.
seeds.limit: V_OV made very small: what does the square law predict, and what really happens near threshold?
seeds.transfer: Two transistors must carry currents in a ratio of 4 to 1 at the same V_GS: what ratio of W/L do you choose?

channel-length-modulation.L1: States I_D = ½μC_ox(W/L)V_OV²(1 + λV_DS) and r_o = 1/(λI_D).
channel-length-modulation.L2: Computes r_o and the change in saturated current for a change in V_DS.
channel-length-modulation.L3: Explains it as the pinch-off point moving toward the source as V_DS grows, shortening the channel; predicts that longer channels have smaller λ and larger r_o; connects it to the copy error of a mirror and the intrinsic gain.
channel-length-modulation.L4: Uses longer L to raise r_o where gain or copy accuracy matters, and knows the cost in area and speed; knows λ itself depends on L.
missteps: writes r_o = λI_D
ignores λ when comparing currents at different V_DS
thinks a longer channel has a larger λ

seeds.predict: Two transistors carry the same current, one twice as long: which has the larger r_o, and by roughly how much?
seeds.explain: Why the saturated current still grows a little with V_DS.
seeds.limit: λ set to zero: what does a saturated transistor become, and which gains become infinite?
seeds.transfer: A current mirror's output must stay within 1 % over a 1 V swing: what λ does that need?
